title: Playing the H&J with Brother Cornbread
summary: He played with Cornbread at 16 and again during the war; he formed a band at his Ordnance company after going in late 1941.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You ever been to the H&J? H&J?
Sure, I played the H&J with Brother Cornbread. Mm-hmm.
there a long time with Brother Cornbread playing H&J.
How old were you at that time?

Well, I was quite a young man. Well, I tell you, when I first played with Brother Cornbread, I probably would have been about 16 years old, but I mean at the H&J, I played with him during the wartime, like uh, like, like, you know, early fotties.
Was that, that would have to be before you went in the service then?

Well, I played with Brother Cornbread before I went to the service, but I mean after I went to the service in the latter part of 41, and I formed a band, they gave me, I didn't go in special service, but my company commander understood it well enough that I had talent, and he let me form a band in the service, myself, right in the club, in our outfit, like 590 Ordnance Ammunition Company, and I toured the whole Philippine Island most. We was in Manila, and I had a band, went to all the sodas, came playing music, and even played the nightclubs. They gave me, my time was off, we played the nightclubs, and gave me transportation.
